newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-LAMA HANDED FIVE-MONTH BAN WITH THREE SUSPENDED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAMA HANDED FIVE-MONTH BAN WITH THREE SUSPENDED.

text.p: Paris St Germain's Bernard Lama became France's second leading goalkeeper in two years to be punished for using cannabis when he was banned for five months, three suspended, by the French Football Federation (FFF) on Thursday.
Monaco's Fabien Barthez, Lama's chief rival for the France goalkeeper's jersey, was banned for four months, serving two, for the same offence in October 1995.

"We took into account the fact that Lama, being popular, should be an example for young people, said Jean-Yves Audureau, president of the FFF's doping commission, to explain why Lama's ban was slightly harsher.
"We also felt that he should have learnt from what happened to Barthez," Audureau said.

Lama, who tested positive for cannabis while training with the French national team in February, will begin the suspension from the moment he receives a letter of notification, expected on Friday, he said.
The goalkeeper, who played for PSG in the European Cup Winners' Cup final against Barcelona in Rotterdam on Wednesday night, has 15 days in which to appeal. PSG lost 1-0.

There is an automatic 10-day period between an appeal and the hearing which could theoretically free Lama to play for PSG in their last two league games of the season, away to Marseille this Saturday and at home to Strasbourg a week later.
But Lama, who was at Thursday's appeal, said he had not decided yet whether to appeal.
"I won't comment before the end of the procedure," he said. I'll take my time to decide whether to appeal. I'm not surprised by the sanction because everybody should know what the law is."

Lama's participation in the World Cup warm-up Tournoi de France from June 3 to 11 will depend only on whether national team boss Aime Jacquet picks him as the ban only applies to matches played by PSG, a FFF spokesman said.
